input_signals.name: AccrualIssuanceComposite
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that simultaneously report accrual-heavy earnings and raise net external capital (equity plus debt, net of repurchases and repayments) are the most likely to be overvalued and to disappoint, because both the accounting and the financing channel signal that reported profits are not self-funding.
input_signals.reasoning: Total accruals (ib minus oancf) measure the non-cash share of earnings, while net external financing measures cash raised from outside claimants; requiring both to be high isolates firms whose growth is funded by capital markets rather than operations. Rank-summing the two channels keeps coverage broad while ensuring the score peaks only when both accounting quality and financing behavior are unfavorable.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ) )

input_signals.name: LeverageAmplifiedAccruals
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(MUL(SUB(ib, oancf), lt), MUL(at, at)), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: A given amount of accrual-based earnings is more dangerous when the balance sheet is already financed with heavy outside liabilities, since low-quality earnings plus a thin equity cushion raises the probability of covenant pressure, forced deleveraging, and future write-offs.
input_signals.reasoning: The expression multiplies scaled accruals by the liability-to-asset financing structure, producing a genuine amplitude interaction: the score is extreme only when soft earnings coincide with high creditor claims. Winsorizing controls the tail leverage of the product without changing the economic ordering.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( mul( sub( ib, oancf ), lt ), mul( at, at ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: ShareIssuedWorkingCapitalBuildup
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), txp)), at), 1)), RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Working-capital expansion (receivables and inventory growth net of operating liabilities) that is accompanied by share-count growth indicates that soft revenue recognition is being financed by diluting existing shareholders, a combination that precedes negative earnings surprises.
input_signals.reasoning: The first rank isolates the non-cash operating accrual buildup after netting out debt-like current items, while the second rank captures equity dilution measured directly from share count rather than cash-flow-statement issuance, giving an independent financing read. The product is high only when the working-capital build is externally equity-funded, which is the overvaluation case.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( sub( lct, dlc ), txp ) ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( growth( csho, 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: PersistentAccrualFinancingPair
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TS_SUM(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 3)), RANK(TS_SUM(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Repeated, multi-year reliance on both accrual-based earnings and external capital identifies chronically cash-deficient firms whose business model is sustained by financing rather than one-off accounting noise, and this persistent combination should be more strongly mispriced than a single-year event.
input_signals.reasoning: Three-year cumulative sums filter transitory accrual reversals and lumpy single financing events, so only firms that repeatedly close a cash gap with outside money score high on both channels. The multiplicative rank structure enforces the joint condition and targets the "serial external funder with soft earnings" archetype.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ts_sum( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 3 ) ), rank( ts_sum( ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: BalanceSheetAccrualNetFinancing
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at), RATIO(ADD(DELTA(dltt, 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), ib)), at))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose working-capital accruals (net of depreciation) are high at the same time that they are raising net debt and net equity are financing non-cash earnings growth from outside capital, and should subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Both legs are built purely from balance-sheet items, with net equity issuance measured as the clean-surplus residual DELTA(ceq) minus earnings, so the signal avoids the cash-flow-statement items that capped prior coverage near 0.08. If the accrual-financing mechanism is real rather than a sample artifact, this construction should reproduce or strengthen the gen-0 composite's FMB slope on a much larger firm-month sample.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( delta( wcap, 1 ), dp ), at ), ratio( add( delta( dltt, 1 ), sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), ib ) ), at ) )

input_signals.name: IndustryNeutralAccrualFinancing
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accrual and issuance intensity are strongly industry-determined (biotech and utilities issue and accrue for structural reasons), so within-industry deviations isolate the firm-specific earnings-management/overvaluation component that is actually mispriced.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-0 composite had a strong FMB slope (−3.72) but weak FF5 alpha (t=−1.88), a pattern consistent with the extreme portfolios loading on a few financing-heavy industries whose common return variation is absorbed by factor exposure and residual volatility. Industry-standardizing each leg before ranking should stabilize portfolio composition and lift ls_talpha without changing the economic channel.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: DebtFundedAccrualCashDrain
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(DELTA(dltt, 1), at), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Balance-sheet pressure is clearest when soft earnings coincide with new long-term borrowing *and* a decline in cash holdings: the firm is consuming liquidity and adding fixed claims while reporting non-cash profits.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike the failed gen-0 stress signal, which used only second-order changes in accruals and dividends, this keeps the accrual level (the leg with proven cross-sectional power) and adds two first-order funding-pressure channels that jointly identify firms whose reported earnings are not replenishing the cash buffer. It tests whether the liquidity-drain dimension adds information beyond issuance volume.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), sumrank( ratio( delta( dltt, 1 ), at ), neg( ratio( delta( che, 1 ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: IndNeutralAccrualDebtCashDrain
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(DELTA(dltt, 1), at)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Soft earnings combined with new long-term borrowing and a falling cash buffer identifies firms whose reported profits are neither cash-generating nor self-financing, and the mispricing is firm-specific rather than industry-driven.
input_signals.reasoning: This merges the two strongest gen-1 results — industry neutralization (best fmb and talpha) and the debt-funded cash-drain channel (largest alpha) — which were previously tested separately, so it directly asks whether their information is additive. If the liquidity-drain leg is not simply a noisy proxy for issuance, industry-standardizing all three legs should raise both fmb_tstat and ls_talpha above either parent.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), sumrank( ind_zscore( ratio( delta( dltt, 1 ), at ) ), ind_zscore( neg( ratio( delta( che, 1 ), at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ConjunctiveAccrualIssuance
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The overvaluation story is genuinely conjunctive: only firms that are simultaneously accrual-aggressive and net external financiers should be shorted, while a firm extreme on one dimension alone carries little information.
input_signals.reasoning: Additive SUMRANK lets one extreme leg dominate, so a highly accrual-heavy firm that repurchases stock still enters the short book; MIN enforces the "both, or neither" logic while staying monotone in each input, avoiding the sign pathology of products and the bin-collapse of the failed indicator version. Comparing it to the additive industry-neutral composite isolates whether the true structure is interaction or two-factor addition.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: IndNeutralAccrualIssuanceLeverage
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(lt, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Financing pressure has both a flow dimension (capital currently being raised) and a stock dimension (existing outside claims); accrual mispricing should be strongest where both are elevated because the firm has little slack to absorb an accrual reversal.
input_signals.reasoning: The leverage-amplified accrual signal produced a reliable alpha (−3.1%, t=−2.29) and the issuance composite a strong slope, but the two financing dimensions have never been used together within industry. Adding the leverage stock as a third industry-standardized leg tests whether balance-sheet capacity is incremental to issuance activity, and rank aggregation avoids the product form that already failed.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), sumrank( ind_zscore( ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( lt, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: PersistentIndNeutralAccrualFinancing
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Chronic dependence on accruals and outside capital, rather than a single fiscal year's realization, identifies structurally cash-deficient firms whose valuations are most likely to be corrected.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-0 persistence test used three-year sums inside a rank product, which conflated the persistence idea with the failed multiplicative form; here persistence is implemented as three-year averages inside the aggregation structure that actually worked. Smoothing should reduce reporting noise and portfolio turnover, so if the mechanism is a chronic state we expect higher ls_talpha and Sharpe than the one-year industry-neutral composite.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_zscore( ma( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 3 ) ), ind_zscore( ma( ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: AccrualsWithShortMaturityDebtReliance
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(dlc, ADD(dlc, dltt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Beyond how much a firm borrows, the maturity mix matters: accrual-heavy firms funded disproportionately with short-term debt face imminent rollover decisions, giving lenders a near-term option to withdraw exactly when accruals reverse.
input_signals.reasoning: Every financing leg tested so far measures volume (issuance, net financing, total liabilities); maturity structure is an untested and economically distinct dimension of financing fragility that requires no cash-flow-statement items. Pairing it with the proven accrual leg inside the industry-neutral rank frame keeps the comparison clean, so a strong result would identify rollover risk, not issuance appetite, as the amplifying mechanism.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( dlc, add( dlc, dltt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: AccrualsWithNetEquityIssuance
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The accrual-financing interaction is an equity-market-timing phenomenon: managers inflate accruals when they intend to sell equity and avoid issuance (or repurchase) when the stock is cheap, so net equity issuance should be the dominant financing leg.
input_signals.reasoning: The winning composite bundles equity and debt flows into one number, which hides whether the mispricing comes from overvaluation (equity channel) or funding pressure (debt channel). Isolating net equity issuance against the proven accrual leg in the proven aggregation frame gives a decisive read on the overvaluation interpretation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: AccrualsWithNetDebtIssuance
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(dltis, dltr), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: If the interaction reflects balance-sheet pressure rather than equity overvaluation, then net long-term debt issuance is the financing action that matters, because creditors ratify soft earnings with fixed claims the firm must service in cash.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the exact counterpart to Signal 1, holding the accrual leg and aggregation fixed so the comparison identifies the operative economic channel rather than a formula variant. Given that the leverage stock helped alpha and payout did not, debt-side financing is a live hypothesis worth separating.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( sub( dltis, dltr ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: AccrualsVsFinancingFragilityIndex
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), RATIO(dlc, ADD(dlc, dltt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Financing vulnerability has a volume dimension (net capital currently raised) and a maturity dimension (reliance on short-term debt that must be rolled); combining them into one index, then interacting with accruals, should dominate either single financing measure.
input_signals.reasoning: The two best FMB slopes in the archive came from accruals paired with net financing (−4.20) and accruals paired with short-maturity reliance (−3.88), and nesting the two financing measures inside the inner SUMRANK keeps the accrual leg at full 50% weight instead of down-weighting it to one third as the failed three-leg versions did. This directly repairs the dilution failure mode observed in generation 2.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), sumrank( ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ), ratio( dlc, add( dlc, dltt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: AccrualEscalationAtIssuance
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Earnings management is an event, not a level: the informative case is a firm whose accruals *jumped* in the same year it raised outside capital, because that is the pattern consistent with dressing up reported earnings for investors.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-0 change-based signal failed, but it used second-order changes, no industry neutralization, and a stress-oriented financing leg; here only the accrual leg is differenced while everything proven is held fixed. If the accrual level leg beats it, we learn the anomaly is about accrual *stock* overstatement rather than a discretionary spike, which sharpens later refinements.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_zscore( delta( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: AccrualsAfterPriorYearFinancing
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_ZSCORE(LAG(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: If the mechanism is post-financing disappointment, the relevant financing already happened: firms that raised capital last year and still report accrual-heavy earnings are the ones facing an imminent reversal with the proceeds already spent.
input_signals.reasoning: Contemporaneous pairing cannot distinguish "manipulating to issue" from "issuing then disappointing," and the three-year smoothing test showed timing matters materially. Lagging only the financing leg by one year isolates the drift interpretation and, if it holds up, also implies the signal is tradable further from the financing event with less stale-accrual overlap.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), ind_zscore( lag( ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_ZSCORE(GROWTH(csho, 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Share-count growth captures all forms of equity dilution — secondary offerings, stock-financed acquisitions, and option exercise — so it should identify accrual-heavy firms paying with overvalued paper even when cash-flow-statement issuance is small.
input_signals.reasoning: Dilution via csho was only tested once, inside the failed rank-product with a weak working-capital accrual leg, so its standalone interaction value is unknown; stock-financed acquisitions are exactly where accrual inflation and overvaluation coincide most strongly. Pairing it with the proven accrual leg in the winning frame tests the "overvalued paper" channel that cash issuance proceeds miss.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), ind_zscore( growth( csho, 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: WorkingCapitalAccrualLegWithNetFinancing
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dpc), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Within the cash-flow accrual measure, it is the working-capital buildup rather than the depreciation offset that reflects discretionary earnings quality, so adding depreciation back should sharpen the accounting-quality leg of the interaction.
input_signals.reasoning: The measure ib − oancf nets working-capital accruals against depreciation, mixing a discretionary manipulation channel with a mechanical capital-intensity channel that is largely industry-determined; adding dpc back isolates the discretionary part while keeping the same cash-flow-statement sample and the proven financing leg. This is the accrual-composition test that failed when attempted with balance-sheet items (wcap, recch/invch), so doing it inside the cash-flow definition tells us whether those failures were measurement artifacts or genuine evidence against the working-capital channel.

input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_zscore( ratio( add( sub( ib, oancf ), dpc ), at ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accrual aggressiveness is best judged against industry peers (accounting norms are industry-specific), whereas financing is best judged against the firm's own funding history (an issuance spike is the event that signals opportunism).
input_signals.reasoning: This hybrid separates the two normalization questions that Signal 2 bundles, so the pair identifies which leg actually benefits from a within-firm frame. It preserves the accrual leg that has generated every strong result while making the financing leg event-like rather than type-like.

input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_ZSCORE(VOL(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Erratic reliance on outside capital indicates an opaque, funding-fragile firm whose reported earnings quality cannot be verified from cash generation; accrual-heavy firms with volatile financing should therefore underperform more than accrual-heavy firms with steady financing policies.
input_signals.reasoning: Every financing leg so far measures the level or direction of financing, never its instability, yet second-moment funding risk is a distinct economic mechanism (rollover and access risk) that does not require the firm to be a net issuer this year. It also tests whether the anomaly needs a directional financing signal at all, which would be informative even if the result is null.

input_signals.name: IssuanceBeyondInternalEarningsWithAccruals
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), ib), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Financing is most suspicious when it far exceeds what the firm's reported earnings could fund: raising outside capital well in excess of internal profits is the signature of opportunistic issuance into a favorable valuation.
input_signals.reasoning: Scaling financing only by assets ignores whether the firm actually needed the money, so subtracting earnings creates an internal-funds-relative financing measure that separates opportunistic raisers from firms plugging a genuine profit shortfall. Because the accrual leg uses cash flow and this leg uses earnings, the two legs remain economically distinct rather than mechanically redundant.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), ind_zscore( ratio( sub( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), ib ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: AccrualsWithCumulativeThreeYearFinancing
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_ZSCORE(TS_SUM(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The stock of recently raised outside capital, accumulated over three years, measures how much of the firm's current balance sheet was funded by investors rather than operations, and current accrual aggressiveness on top of that stock signals the coming correction.
input_signals.reasoning: When both legs were smoothed in generation 2 the signal weakened, but that test confounded stale accruals with accumulated financing; accumulating only the financing leg keeps the accrual information fresh while capturing multi-year external funding intensity. This isolates whether the earlier smoothing failure came from the accrual leg's staleness, as I suspect, rather than from persistence per se.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), ind_zscore( ts_sum( ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at)), TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accrual-heavy firms are most mispriced when they are both structurally dependent on outside capital (high versus industry peers) and raising unusually much versus their own funding history, because the first identifies the vulnerable business model and the second identifies the opportunistic event.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's two frontier signals differ only in how the financing leg is normalized, and each dominates a different metric, which implies the two frames carry complementary information rather than substituting for each other. Averaging them inside the financing leg keeps the accrual leg at full 50% weight, so this should recover the strong FMB slope of the cross-sectional version while retaining the superior Sharpe of the event version.

input_signals.hypothesis: The sharpest version of the story is a working-capital-driven earnings overstatement funded by capital raised well in excess of what the firm actually earned — discretionary accounting on the asset side, opportunistic financing on the liability side.
input_signals.reasoning: Generation 4 validated each leg refinement separately against the same benchmark — depreciation add-back on the accrual side and internal-funds-relative scaling on the financing side — but never jointly, so this tests whether their improvements are additive or overlapping. input_signals.name: IndRankAccrualFinancing
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The economic content of the interaction is ordinal — being an accrual-aggressive, capital-raising firm relative to peers — so within-industry percentile ranks should represent it more robustly than z-scores, which are distorted by the extreme scaled ratios of small, low-asset firms.
input_signals.reasoning: IND_ZSCORE standardizes by an industry standard deviation that is itself dominated by a handful of extreme observations, which can make the tails of the sorted portfolio unstable and depress ls_talpha relative to the underlying slope. This is a deliberate single-choice isolation of the standardization operator on the archive's best signal, and its outcome tells later generations whether outlier control or economic content is the binding constraint on portfolio evidence.

input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ind_rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dvt, prstkc), ib), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Distributing more cash to shareholders than the firm earned, while earnings are already accrual-inflated, indicates a payout being sustained by outside capital or balance-sheet depletion rather than by real profits.
input_signals.reasoning: The earlier payout test measured only the *absence* of distributions and was weak, but over-distribution relative to reported earnings is the economically opposite and much more informative condition, since it forces the firm back to the capital markets. This keeps the proven accrual leg fixed so the test cleanly evaluates a payout-sustainability channel that the issuance-volume legs cannot capture.

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms continuously transacting with capital markets in both directions are habitually dependent on external validation and face recurring incentives to present favorable earnings, so gross financing turnover should amplify accrual mispricing even when net flows are near zero.
input_signals.reasoning: Every financing leg tested so far is directional (net issuance, payout, maturity, trend), and the one gross-flow attempt was crippled by the multiplicative form that failed for unrelated reasons; as a ranked leg, gross churn is an untested and economically distinct measure of capital-market engagement. input_signals.hypothesis: The short side requires both conditions simultaneously — inflated accruals and distributions exceeding cash generation — so a multiplicative rank interaction should concentrate the mispricing in the extreme portfolio better than an additive average.
input_signals.reasoning: The earlier conjunction test used MIN on z-scores and produced a good slope but a weak spread because MIN discards all information once one leg is low; a product of within-industry percentile ranks stays smooth and monotone in both legs while still requiring joint extremity. Applying it to the now-best leg pair tests whether the interaction is genuinely multiplicative, which is the central economic claim of this theme pairing.

input_signals.hypothesis: Accrual aggressiveness interacts separately with over-distribution and with external funding dependence, so averaging the two interaction terms should retain full interaction strength while diversifying the portfolio across two distinct financing red flags.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding the issuance leg additively to the payout leg previously produced the best Sharpe in the archive (−0.54), which says the two channels are imperfectly correlated sources of the same economic signal. Averaging the two *products* rather than the two levels preserves the conjunctive structure that generated the −3.73 alpha t-stat while capturing that diversification benefit.

input_signals.hypothesis: The most extreme case is a firm that is accrual-aggressive, distributing beyond its operating cash flow, and simultaneously raising outside capital — recycling investor money while reporting non-cash profits.
input_signals.reasoning: If the mechanism is genuinely conjunctive, adding a third bounded rank should further concentrate the short leg on the pathological cases, whereas if it merely narrows the sample it will show up as a weaker slope with an unstable spread. input_signals.hypothesis: Total dependence on outside claimholders — capital taken in plus distributions not covered by operations — is one economic quantity, and accrual aggressiveness should be multiplied by that single composite rather than by each component separately.
input_signals.reasoning: Summing the two financing ratios before ranking gives the firm's overall external-claim burden in comparable asset-scaled units, so the interaction remains a clean two-way product with only one financing dimension to rank. input_signals.reasoning: The champion counts only shareholder distributions, yet scheduled debt repayment is an equally non-discretionary cash outflow, and creditor claims are precisely where balance-sheet pressure becomes binding. input_signals.reasoning: Scaling by assets treats a cash-rich and a cash-poor firm with the same gap identically, whereas the economic mechanism is a runway calculation; the within-industry rank transformation makes the small-denominator instability of this ratio harmless.
